testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is the thin layer of ice that forms on road surfaces called?
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice on the road. You can see the road surface through it. A road with black ice looks wet. Be very careful when the temperature is below freezing and the road appears wet.

questions.question: How should you warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down?

options.text: Turn on the right turn signal, then the left turn signal
Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights
Swerve from side to side to get their attention

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to flash your brake lights. This tells drivers behind you that you plan to slow down. It is important to communicate your actions to other drivers.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor fails, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always best
So they do not lose control of their vehicle
So they do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead
To be the last vehicle through an intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: So they do not lose control of their vehicle
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on a road with poor traction can cause you to lose control. In poor-traction conditions, accelerate smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: When does front wheel braking work?

options.text: Only if the road is dry

questions.explanation: Front wheel braking works in all road conditions. Front wheel skids are rare, even on ice.

questions.question: What is true about the pre-trip vehicle inspection test?

options.text: Applicants do not have to identify the ABS
Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle
The steering box should be checked for leaks

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering box should be checked for leaks
questions.explanation: During the external pre-trip inspection, you must check that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles transporting hazardous materials
They are illegal in most states
They help drivers see a larger area

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers see a larger area
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved, convex mirrors. Convex mirrors allow you to see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: What is true about dry bulk tanks?

options.text: They usually have low centers of gravity
They usually have high centers of gravity
They are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks
They cannot be driven on interstates

questions.correctAnswerText: They usually have high centers of gravity
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity and require special care. The materials inside can shift during transit, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: What is one way to avoid a hazard?

options.text: You should always steer to the left
You may be able to drive onto the shoulder
You should steer sharply in one direction

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be able to drive onto the shoulder
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: Why should a driver accelerate slowly on a surface with poor traction?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly
To keep from losing control of the vehicle
So that they do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle
questions.explanation: Accelerate slowly in poor-traction conditions such as rain or snow to avoid losing control of your vehicle.

questions.question: The steering wheel should move no more than:
questions.explanation: Too much steering wheel movement (more than 10 degrees) makes it hard to steer the vehicle.

questions.question: During the driving test, what should you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while your vehicle is on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Brake drums are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that make the vehicle stop are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: How often should you check the cargo you are transporting?

options.text: Only at the start of the trip.
Only after driving a long distance.

questions.explanation: Check the cargo and how it is secured before starting your trip. After you begin driving, check it again within the first 50 miles, then every 3 hours or 150 miles, and after every break.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that ____ turn on automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should turn on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Test this by blocking the wheels and releasing air from the brake system by pressing and releasing the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes turn on.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo, no matter how small, must have a minimum of two tie-downs.

questions.question: The only way to become sober after drinking alcohol is to:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol from your body at a fixed rate. Cold showers or coffee cannot speed up this process. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) fails, what happens?

options.text: The truck can only drive at slow speeds.
The truck loses brakes on the left side.

questions.explanation: If ABS fails, the vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: Which tire condition is NOT a problem?

options.text: Tread depth of at least 4/32 inch on front tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread depth of at least 4/32 inch on front tires
questions.explanation: Check tires for: incorrect air pressure, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, tread depth less than 4/32 inch on front tires, and tread depth less than 2/32 inch on all other tires.

questions.question: What should you do when confronted by an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: Do not respond to an aggressive driver's angry gestures. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Remove wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test the warning signal by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brake system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?
questions.explanation: Always check that your service brakes work properly before you drive. Testing the brakes before each trip helps you find problems before you need to stop on the road.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: The state will tell your employer.

questions.explanation: If you are convicted of any traffic violation in any vehicle, you must notify your employer within 30 days. You must also tell your motor vehicle licensing agency within 30 days if the conviction happened in another state. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need to be in an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR)?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. Required information includes the trip start and end points and the Vehicle Identification Number. The number of meals eaten is not required.

questions.question: What is traction?

options.text: Friction between the tires and the road
The time it takes for brakes to work

questions.correctAnswerText: Friction between the tires and the road
questions.explanation: Traction is the grip between your tires and the road. Good traction is needed for braking and steering.

questions.question: How do you stop a vehicle with air brakes?
questions.explanation: To stop normally in a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. The harder you push, the more air pressure is released.

questions.question: What does an air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the air storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the air storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: How can a commercial motor vehicle driver use a cell phone while driving?

options.text: A driver may use any cell phone while driving.
A driver may only use a hands-free cell phone if allowed.
A driver may only use a cell phone on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may only use a hands-free cell phone if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving a commercial motor vehicle, use only a hands-free phone placed near you. Even a hands-free phone can distract you from driving. Know all cell phone laws in the states where you drive.

questions.question: An air brake vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about how many feet to stop?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs about 450 feet to stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which one do you NOT have to do?

options.text: Complete the test without a moving violation.
Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Obey all traffic signs and signals only when other cars are present.
questions.explanation: You must drive safely during the on-road test. This means wearing your safety belt, obeying all traffic signs and signals at all times, obeying all traffic laws, and avoiding accidents or moving violations.

questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the road shoulder:

options.text: May be focused on fixing the vehicle and not watching traffic.
Does not have to follow traffic laws.
Should not be helped by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on fixing the vehicle and not watching traffic.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people fixing disabled vehicles. They are focused on their repair work and may not notice traffic or other dangers on the road.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be fixed, but not urgently.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. A broken suspension is very dangerous and must be repaired immediately.

questions.question: A 40-foot item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. All cargo needs at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: Too much air pressure in a tire:
questions.explanation: Never overinflate your tires. Check tire pressure with a gauge during vehicle inspections.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a good way to prevent crashes when turning right?

options.text: Keep the rear of your vehicle close to the curb.
Leave open space on your right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave open space on your right side.
questions.explanation: When turning right, do not turn too wide to the left. Keep your vehicle's rear close to the curb. Leaving space on your right side while turning right may confuse other drivers into thinking you are turning left, and they may try to pass on your right.

questions.question: When driving in fog, a driver should:
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When the road is wet, a lack of spray from other vehicles' tires means:

options.text: Ice has formed on the road.
The spray is trapped under the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ice has formed on the road.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, if you see no spray coming from other vehicles' tires, ice has formed on the road. Be extra careful when driving in wet, freezing weather.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT another name for convex mirrors?
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are also called "fisheye," "spot," or "bug-eye" mirrors.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is broken?

options.text: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes can leak from the muffler.
It can cause problems when the trailer is full.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can allow poisonous fumes to enter your cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system regularly for damage.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light shows that the ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) is broken and needs service.

questions.question: When parked on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear flashing lights.
Use one set of turn signals.

questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is very important at night.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
A lack of oil in the engine.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is dangerous. It can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper area.

questions.question: What is a Gross Vehicle Weight Rating?

options.text: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a vehicle can weigh when fully loaded
The maximum weight that can be pulled by a single vehicle
The minimum weight that can be hauled by a single vehicle
The maximum amount that can be loaded onto a single trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum weight the manufacturer says a vehicle can weigh when fully loaded
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum weight the manufacturer states for a vehicle and its load combined.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
Keeps the load the proper distance behind the driver's compartment.
Maintains a safe distance between the vehicle and other vehicles.
Lightens the load for the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Holds up the vehicle and its load.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its load and keeps the axles in place. A broken suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, you should:

options.text: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accept it and drive at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, manage your stress. If you will be late, accept it and drive safely.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to make the brakes work?
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles use air brakes. These brakes work by using compressed air.

questions.question: Sometimes, when checking the automatic transmission fluid level:

options.text: Your vehicle should be parked uphill.
Your vehicle should be parked downhill.
Your vehicle may have to be left running.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle may have to be left running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you must leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When starting the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating level.

questions.question: A danger of swerving to avoid a hazard while driving a large truck is that:

options.text: The truck may miss the object.
The truck may stay in the same lane.

questions.explanation: Swerving is sometimes necessary to avoid hazards, but it has risks. Top-heavy vehicles and tractors with multiple trailers may flip over if they swerve.
